briefing.quote: Once agents start making decisions on our behalf, the value of tools shifts from "boosting efficiency" to "carrying accountability" — whoever controls the auditable execution chain controls the next wave of entry points.

articles.title: OpenClaw v0.9.4 Released: Built-in Sandbox Execution and Tiered Permissions, Agent Actions Now Reversible
articles.summary: The new version introduces a process-level sandbox and a fine-grained permission model, with all tool calls recordable, replayable, and reversible.
articles.detail: The OpenClaw community pushed v0.9.4 this week, with a focus on hardening the secure execution chain: a new syscall-level sandbox with separate permission tiers for file writes, network requests, and command execution; all tool calls are recorded as an append-only event stream, allowing users to roll back to any point in time with one click. A new memory snapshot feature also lets users export long-term memory as JSON for cross-device sync. Officials say this is the final major release before enterprise intranet deployments.
articles.impact: Tiered permissions plus reversible actions give OpenClaw the basic compliance capabilities needed to enter enterprise environments, potentially accelerating domestic Agent frameworks' shift from personal toys to team infrastructure, and creating differentiated competition against LangChain, AutoGen, and others.

articles.title: OpenClaw Plugin Marketplace Opens Public Beta, 320+ Skills Listed in First Week
articles.summary: The official Skill Registry launches with one-click installs, version pinning, and signature verification, with the first wave focused on office automation and data analysis.
articles.detail: OpenClaw's plugin marketplace (Skill Registry) has entered public beta, allowing developers to publish skill packages in .clawpkg format, with the platform offering semantic search, ratings, and dependency resolution. The first batch of over 320 skills covers scenarios such as Notion automation, Feishu multidimensional spreadsheets, Excel batch processing, SQL generation, and resume screening. Officials also released a revenue-sharing plan: 15% commission on paid Skills, with open-source Skills eligible for traffic support. Three domestic SaaS vendors have already integrated with the official certification channel.
articles.impact: The plugin marketplace addresses the pain point of fragmented capabilities and low reuse rates in the Agent ecosystem. Once network effects take hold, OpenClaw evolves from a framework into a distribution platform, creating a new traffic entry point for both indie developers and vertical SaaS providers.

articles.title: Field Test: OpenClaw Multi-Agent Orchestration Automates Weekly Reports, Cutting Time from 2 Hours to 8 Minutes
articles.summary: An evaluation team used a Planner+Coder+Reviewer three-role orchestration to complete the full pipeline of data collection, analysis, and writing.
articles.detail: An enterprise efficiency lab published a real-world test of OpenClaw's multi-agent orchestration: an Orchestrator assigned three roles — Planner (task decomposition), Coder (scripting data scraping), and Reviewer (proofreading output) — completing a market weekly report with five charts in 8 minutes, with a 92% human review pass rate. Failures were mainly concentrated in chart color schemes and Chinese text layout details. The test also noted a token cost of about 3.8 yuan per run, two orders of magnitude lower than manual outsourcing.
articles.impact: Multi-agent orchestration is beginning to produce quantifiable ROI, proving that 'AI employees' are no longer just a concept. Enterprise procurement decisions will shift from 'whether to use AI' to 'which department adopts it first,' reshaping collaboration in HR and operations roles.

articles.title: Skill Trend: Computer Use Agents Top the Weekly Download Growth Chart
articles.summary: Skill packs that let AI directly operate GUIs grew 420% week over week, with office software automation as the main use case.
articles.detail: Data from multiple skill marketplaces shows that "computer-use" skill packs (screenshot recognition + mouse/keyboard simulation + state machine orchestration) ranked first in weekly growth, up 420% week over week. The typical use case is having agents handle tasks on "legacy systems without APIs" — such as ERP order entry, OA approval workflows, and bulk operations on cross-border e-commerce backends. The current mainstream implementation uses a three-layer structure of vision large models + screen coordinate regression + failure retry, with success rates ranging from 78% to 91%. Open-source projects SkyOperator and UI-TARS-skill have been forked extensively.
articles.impact: Computer operation skills open up the largest existing market of "systems without APIs," putting RPA vendors under replacement pressure while creating new monetization opportunities for developers who can write state machines and understand business workflows.

articles.title: "Long-Context Memory Management" Skill Packs Go Viral, Solving the Problem of Agents Getting Dumber Over Time
articles.summary: Skill implementations based on RAG + layered memory deliver cross-session consistency, with a marked improvement in user retention.
articles.detail: Memory management skill packs such as MemoryVault and MemLayer have landed on recommendation slots this week. The core idea is to split memory into three layers — working memory (current task), episodic memory (historical events), and semantic memory (user preferences) — and use vector retrieval plus time-decay scoring to decide which context to inject. Testing shows that in customer service scenarios, the share of users repeating their problem description dropped 63%, and task completion rates in long conversations rose by 27 percentage points. Some implementations already support exporting memory as editable Markdown, letting users "train" their agents themselves.
articles.impact: The memory layer is critical infrastructure for taking agents from demos to long-term companionship. Teams that master memory standards will build a moat around user stickiness, while also raising a new product and compliance issue: "AI personality assets."

articles.title: Is Prompt Engineering Fading? "Agent Evaluation Skills" Become a Must-Have for Teams
articles.summary: Demand has surged for automated regression testing and evaluator orchestration skills, as enterprises begin paying for quality.
articles.detail: As agents move into production environments, "one change breaks everything" has become a common pain point. This week, search volume for evaluation skill packs such as LangEval-skill and PromptTest has doubled. Features include: building golden datasets, automated regression testing, LLM-as-Judge multi-dimensional scoring, online A/B testing, and cost monitoring. Multiple teams report that introducing an evaluation pipeline actually sped up version iteration by 40%, since manual line-by-line output verification is no longer needed. In the job market, the median salary for "AI evaluation engineer" roles has reached 35K RMB per month.
articles.impact: Evaluation capability determines whether enterprises will keep buying agents — it is the watershed between "it runs" and "it works." Generalists with evaluation methodology will replace pure prompt engineers as the new scarce talent.

articles.title: iOS 26.2 Beta Introduces 'App Intent Permission Panel,' Requiring Siri App Calls to Disclose Data Flows
articles.summary: System-level agent permission visualization lets users see which data AI has accessed and revoke access at any time.
articles.detail: iOS 26.2 Beta adds a permission panel for App Intents: any app capability invoked by Siri, Shortcuts, or third-party agents now generates an auditable record in Settings, showing the type of data read, call frequency, and where results are sent. Developers must declare data usage for each Intent, or face rejection by App Review. A new 'Agent Mode' toggle also allows users to grant a given AI assistant batch app operations for a limited time window.
articles.impact: Apple is setting ground rules for the agent ecosystem in a privacy-controlled way, effectively raising the barrier to entry for third-party AI assistants. Small and mid-sized developers need to adopt the Intent declaration spec quickly, or risk losing their Siri entry point after iOS 26.2 ships.

articles.title: Breakout App Store Hit This Week: On-Device AI Diary App 'Xuyu' Tops One Million Downloads in Seven Days
articles.summary: Features on-device small-model voice-to-diary plus emotion analysis, with an 18% subscription conversion rate, hitting No. 1 in multiple country rankings.
articles.detail: Chinese-built app 'Xuyu' topped the overall charts in China, Japan, and Singapore this week. The product logic is simple: users speak a short message before bed, a Whisper-class on-device model transcribes it, and a local small model generates a structured diary and emotion curve — all data stays on the device. Its subscription page carries a single line, 'Your secrets are never uploaded,' driving an 18% conversion rate, far above the 5% tool-category average. The four-person team spends everything on model fine-tuning and ASR noise reduction.
articles.impact: It proves that 'on-device + privacy narrative + minimalist interaction' remains the golden formula for paid iOS products. It also signals to developers: rather than competing on all-purpose AI assistants, it is better to achieve ultimate trust in a single high-frequency scenario.

articles.title: Apple Intelligence Opens New APIs: Apps Can Subscribe to System-Level Summarization and Semantic Search
articles.summary: Third-party apps can call system models for content summarization and Spotlight semantic indexing, saving on self-built inference costs.
articles.detail: Apple has opened SummaryKit and SemanticIndex API sets to developers: the former lets apps hand long texts, emails, and meeting notes to system models for summarization, while the latter allows in-app content to be hit directly by Spotlight semantic search. Calls are billed per use but at rates far below self-built inference, and data is by default not used for training. Note-taking and podcast apps have already integrated them, with reports citing roughly 70% lower cloud inference costs. The China region is delayed for compliance reasons, expected to roll out alongside iOS 26.2.
articles.impact: System-level AI capabilities are trickling down, significantly lowering the bar for AI features among small and mid-sized developers. At the same time, it pulls 'AI differentiation' back into Apple's hands, and app competition will refocus on product experience and data assets.

articles.title: Zhizao Intelligence Raises $300M Series A to Bring Agents into Manufacturing Quality Control
articles.summary: Vision LLM + industrial control protocols achieve 99.2% defect detection accuracy, already deployed at three leading contract manufacturers.
articles.detail: Shenzhen-based Zhizao Intelligence announced completion of a 200 million yuan Series A round led by a top industrial fund. The company focuses on quality inspection in 3C manufacturing: replacing traditional rule-based algorithms with vision large models for defect detection, and using Agents to automatically trigger sorting, rework and work order dispatch, forming a closed loop. Deployed on production lines at three contract manufacturers, it has achieved 99.2% accuracy, a 65% reduction in false positives, and roughly 1.8 million yuan in annual labor cost savings per line. Core team members come from Foxconn Automation and SenseTime.
articles.impact: 'AI + industrial closed loop' is one of the few sectors where ROI can be clearly calculated today; capital is shifting from general-purpose large models toward vertical deployment. For hardware integrators and process engineers, it represents a new high-value transformation path.

articles.title: Startup Watch: AI Legal Assistant Panzhun Tops 80 Million Yuan ARR in Six Months, Targeting SME Compliance
articles.summary: Contract review + regulatory tracking + self-risk assessment; low ticket price but 89% renewal rate.
articles.detail: Legal AI startup Panzhun disclosed data: ARR surpassed 80 million yuan within 18 months of launch, with 4,300 paying companies and an 89% renewal rate. The product packages contract review, policy tracking and compliance self-assessment into a SaaS product priced at 20,000 yuan per year, far below traditional legal counsel fees. Its moat comes from a self-built database of 1.2 million court judgments and local regulatory rules, plus a continuously human-labeled evaluation set. It has recently begun expanding into Southeast Asia, adapting for cross-border trade compliance.
articles.impact: Compliance is the B2B scenario where AI is most readily endorsed by CFOs. Panzhun's success shows that 'vertical data + clear payer + quantifiable risk reduction' is a reliable path to commercializing AI applications.

articles.title: New AI Hardware: Wearable Recorder Maker EchoPie Raises $50M
articles.summary: Card-sized recorder + real-time transcription + action item extraction, targeting workplace meetings, with hardware gross margin above 50%.
articles.detail: EchoPie has raised 50 million dollars. Its product is a recording card that clips onto a badge, paired with a mobile app for real-time transcription, meeting minutes and task generation, supporting mixed recordings in Chinese, English, Japanese and Korean. Its business model is 'one-time hardware + subscription service,' with hardware gross margin above 50% and subscription ARPU of roughly 300 yuan per year. It is now on the procurement lists of over 300 companies, and overseas crowdfunding has topped 20 million dollars. The controversy centers on recording compliance and workplace trust boundaries.
articles.impact: AI hardware has again validated the subscription model in 'high-frequency, must-have, data-sensitive' scenarios. However, compliance and ethical disputes around recording devices will intensify as adoption spreads; enterprises should establish usage policies in advance before procurement.

hotProjects.quote: You don't chase a trend; you wait until the infrastructure matures and happen to be standing in the right place.
hotProjects.summary: Today's biggest trend: Agents moving from "can chat" to "can be accountable" — auditable, rollback-able and evaluable execution infrastructure has become the shared focus of capital and developers.

projects.name: OpenClaw Skill Registry (Agent Skill Distribution Platform)
projects.oneLiner: The "App Store" of the Agent era — signing, distributing and monetizing skills.
projects.whyHot: OpenClaw's user base is expanding fast, with 320+ skill packages listed in the first week of public beta and a clear developer revenue-share model. Once agent skills become tradable assets, the first-mover platform captures the distribution ecosystem's upside, backed by strong network effects and switching costs.
highlights: Skill package signature verification and version pinning
Dual-track strategy: 15% revenue share plus open-source traffic support
B2B paid conversion via enterprise verification channels
Cross-framework compatibility (whether it supports standards like MCP)
projects.riskTip: Platform depends on a single framework; if OpenClaw ships a major version update or the community splits, skill assets could face compatibility risk. The standards war is far from settled.

projects.name: Computer Use Agent (GUI Automation)
projects.oneLiner: Let AI drive the mouse and keyboard directly, capturing the vast legacy system market without APIs.
projects.whyHot: Skill downloads surged 420% this week, directly tapping into the multi-hundred-billion RPA market. After breakthroughs in vision models, success rates have reached usable levels (78%–91%), with cross-border e-commerce, ERP and OA systems — all API-less — as the first landing scenarios.
highlights: Convergence of vision models plus coordinate regression as a technical approach
Engineering solutions for failure retry and state machine orchestration
Replacement cost comparison versus traditional RPA vendors
Operation auditing and accidental-input prevention safety mechanisms
projects.riskTip: GUI operations are inherently fragile — any interface redesign breaks them. For account permission and financial transactions, liability boundaries and risk control remain enterprises' biggest procurement concerns.

projects.name: Agent Evaluation and Observability Infrastructure
projects.oneLiner: Give AI employees "performance reviews" — a prerequisite for enterprise procurement.
projects.whyHot: Once agents enter production, "fix one thing, break ten" becomes a common pain point. Skill package searches have doubled, and AI evaluation engineer salaries have hit 35K RMB. This is a hard bottleneck from demo to commercial use, with strong willingness to pay and short decision chains.
highlights: Golden dataset construction and automated regression testing
Online A/B testing and token cost monitoring
Compliance audit logs and accountability tracing
projects.riskTip: This sits at the tooling layer and can easily be absorbed "along the way" by foundation model vendors or cloud platforms. Barriers must come from industry benchmark suites and private deployments, or margins will be squeezed.

projects.name: On-Device Privacy AI Apps (diary/companion products like "Xuyu")
projects.oneLiner: Data never leaves the device + minimalist interaction + strong emotional value — the new iOS paid-app formula.
projects.whyHot: "Xuyu" passed 1 million downloads in 7 days with an 18% subscription conversion rate, proving the business model with a 4-person team. Falling on-device model costs combined with growing user privacy anxiety make "local AI + a trust narrative" the most viable startup wedge for small teams.
highlights: Quantization and power optimization of small on-device models
Voice ASR noise reduction and structured output quality
Balancing subscription pricing with emotional value
Whether it can extend to high-trust scenarios like health and parenting
projects.riskTip: Low barriers to entry invite rapid copying and product homogenization. Retention depends on long-term emotional connection; without data accumulation and community, month-two retention can decay fast.
